sections.what: Bayou City Waterkeeper uses science, law and community partnerships to protect water and reduce flooding in the Lower Galveston Bay watershed. Its work includes sewage accountability, wetlands protection and advocacy for infrastructure in underserved communities. This deep review models a conditional sewage-accountability channel, not all flood, wetland or industrial-risk work.
sections.monitoring: Ask for completed lateral repairs or improved public milestones, distinct affected households, repeat exposure episodes and residual repair spending versus mandatory city action. Verify the campaign’s public appropriation, delivery, coalition contribution and net utility-bill or taxpayer costs. The 2025 report pages 10–12 and 29 were visually reviewed; no recipient causal clinical cohort was found.
sections.qualitative: A specific implementation and affordability gap remains beyond mandatory public sewer upgrades. Current monitoring, legal advocacy and community coalition work provide a plausible accountability mechanism. Original epidemiology supports sewage exposure as an acute health risk, although it does not measure this charity’s effect. The $20 million lateral-repair fund is a campaign demand, not delivered repairs or proven cash capacity. Household reach, clinical utility, implementation probability and recipient additionality remain judgments rather than measured causal outcomes. The full annual recipient cost is compared with one partial channel; public costs, other portfolio benefits and the next gift response are unresolved. The legal recipient remains EIN 26-0187498.
sections.cost:
Initial $28.28M → current $26.69M per better life (ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents), with health 0.259638 and signed net resource equivalents 0.222612. The small improvement reflects separating actual advocacy burdens from potential downstream beneficiaries, not evidence of higher effectiveness or a delivered $20M fund. Full FY2024 recognized recipient cost remains $1,287,349. The baseline is public enforcement, required city investment, other advocates and ordinary repair decisions. The 20,000 household opportunity envelope, 0.2 policy success × 0.5 implementation × 0.1 recipient attribution, 30% clinical response, 0.002 utility gain and three years of avoided recurring exposure after a two-year delay are retained transparent hypotheses. Original South Carolina case-crossover evidence links overflows to acute GI diagnoses over 0–4 days, not a measured QALY coefficient. Atlanta infrastructure lowered overflow frequency, but the study did not establish a protective change in the per-event GI association; neither study directly estimates Houston advocacy effects. A one-season clinical sensitivity challenges durability rather than assuming acute illness lasts three years.

Of 200 expected additional household exposures addressed, 40 have a hypothesized $1,000 one-time otherwise-paid repair saving; positive gains receive 0.5 overlap adjustment. This is genuine avoided resource expenditure only if households would otherwise pay, not public expenditure or a subsidy automatically treated as net welfare. One welfare adult-equivalent per household and $30,000 annual consumption are judgments. An independently judged 100 engaged household-equivalent cohort bears $20 effort costs and 0.00005 process-stress harm regardless of success; potential beneficiaries are not automatically advocates. Random-overlap judgment partitions households into 0.2 changed participants, 39.8 changed nonparticipants and 99.8 other participants. Same-household same-year gains and costs enter one joint log, with all negative costs retained. Immediate effort costs are logged at year zero for all 100 engaged households, while repair savings are logged at year two for 40 expected responders. Different-year welfare is discounted separately, never capitalizing costs inside a future log. When costs and gains occur in the same year, overlapping household and payer components are jointly logged. Houston share 0.8 is applied once.

Distinct payer losses test repair subsidies, compliance resources, taxes and utility bills; central zero external loss is unknown-neutral, not measured absence. The historical $2B over 15 years is required public investment, neither charity income nor household benefit. The advocacy-only recognized cost sensitivity $309,173 excludes overhead, education and other services and is not a verified sewage allocation or marginal gift. The 2025 report’s rounded revenue less net asset change implies roughly $1.138M expense only as an unaudited inference sensitivity. Wetlands, flood resilience and industrial-risk outcomes remain unknown, not zero. The reference is full recipient cost versus partial sewage benefits, not complete portfolio EV.
sections.funding: Current donations use the official legal recipient. Rounded 2025 net assets and cash indicate organizational resources, not unrestricted capacity or the marginal effect of another donation; request a restricted campaign budget, delivery milestones and alternative funding.

model.costScope: Full FY2024 recipient cost versus one annual conditional sewage-compliance channel; not complete portfolio EV or marginal gift.
model.geographicAttribution: Lower Galveston Bay watershed with judged Houston metro share 0.8.
model.formula: Health = clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted years minus full independent engaged-cohort process harm, localized once. Resources = disjoint household joint logs with positive-only overlap, full negative burdens and distinct payer incidence. Price = 10 × annual cost / combined equivalents only if positive.
model.counterfactual: Federal/state enforcement, mandatory city upgrades, other advocates and ordinary privately paid repairs without BCWK; existing public $2B obligations are baseline, not the recipient’s new benefit.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded annual finance and campaign stage; every reach/probability/utility/duration/resource mapping remains judgment. Clinical studies establish risk mechanisms, not local charity causal coefficients. Complete portfolio and marginal-gift EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Monitoring and coalition advocacy; $20M lateral fund is demanded, not delivered. The 2025 annual report describes public implementation gaps and statewide funding possibility, not unique completed recipient-caused household outcomes.
